questions.q: What does `azurerm_mssql_server` combined with `azurerm_mssql_database` provision, in Terraform's AzureRM provider?
options: An Azure SQL Database (PaaS) — a logical server and a database on it, without you managing the underlying OS
A Kubernetes cluster running containerized SQL Server
An on-premises SQL Server failover cluster
A full virtual machine with SQL Server manually installed
questions.explain: These are the AzureRM provider's first-class resources for Azure SQL Database, a PaaS offering.

questions.q: What is the practical benefit of running `terraform plan` before `terraform apply`?
options: It deletes all existing resources first
It skips the need for a resource_group entirely
It shows exactly what will be created or changed before anything actually touches the cloud provider
It automatically fixes any errors in the configuration file
questions.explain: Plan is a dry run that previews the change so it can be reviewed before it's actually applied.

questions.q: What is the key difference between provisioning Azure SQL Database (PaaS) versus a SQL Server VM (IaaS)?
options: With PaaS, Microsoft manages the OS and SQL Server binaries; with IaaS, you own the VM's OS-level configuration and patching
PaaS is always cheaper regardless of workload
There is no real difference — the terms are interchangeable
IaaS cannot be provisioned using Terraform at all
questions.explain: That operational-ownership boundary is the real, practical distinction between the two approaches.

questions.q: Why does the lesson use `var.sql_admin_password` instead of a literal password string in the Terraform resource block?
options: Passwords are automatically generated by Azure and cannot be set
Terraform doesn't support string literals in resource blocks
Variables are required syntax for every Terraform attribute
Real IaC for SQL Server almost never hardcodes secrets directly in the file — values come from a secrets store or variable input instead
questions.explain: Parameterizing secrets and environment-specific values, rather than hardcoding them, is standard real-world IaC practice.

questions.q: If a team needs full instance-level SQL Server control not exposed by Azure SQL Database, which provisioning path do they need, and what do they take on by choosing it?
options: IaC cannot provision any option that offers full instance-level control
PaaS, because it always exposes every instance-level setting
IaaS — a VM running SQL Server — and with it the responsibility for OS-level patching and configuration
Neither path supports this; it requires manual portal configuration only
questions.explain: Choosing IaaS for full control means the team now owns what a PaaS offering would otherwise handle for them.
